brief: Brent crude spiked to $118 on Oct 30 on fears of post-midterm Gulf escalation, then fell to just under $98 by week's end, its steepest weekly drop since April 2020 and biggest in dollar terms since 1988, after a Democratic sweep, Trump signaling no immediate strikes, and a Qatari call eased war-premium pricing. Goldman's Robert Quinn (CFTC COT data) finds Managed Money sold $6.6bn of Brent Oct 27-Nov 3, the 7th time in 5 years notional selling topped $6bn, three-quarters of it liquidation rather than new shorts. Net length fell from about $28bn in October to about $19bn by Nov 4, versus over $45bn in April. The window excludes Wednesday's 8.7% crash, when the sweep raised doubts about funding overseas operations and short-term CTA momentum flipped negative, so next week's COT should look worse. Quinn's history shows 3 prior similar liquidations each preceded 2 further weeks of selling, but one counterexample (2024 OPEC) reversed fully after policymaker pushback. Quinn flags options already buying calls again. UBS's Ellis counters that inventory drawdowns and Hormuz risk still floor prices, and fresh US strikes on Iran followed a Friday peace call.
